Arrange the sentence parts:

(A) announced

(B) the winner

(C) was

(D) yesterday evening
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option (1)** i.e. **BCAD**.

• The logical order of sentence parts is determined by the subject, verb, and other sentence elements.
 
• Part **(B)** “the winner” serves as the subject of the sentence.
 
• Part **(C)** “was” acts as the helping verb connecting the subject to the action.
 
• Part **(A)** “announced” is the main verb describing the action.
 
• Part **(D)** “yesterday evening” tells when the action took place and thus comes at the end.
 
• Hence, the correct sequence is **BCAD**, forming the sentence: *“The winner was announced yesterday evening.”*

Therefore, the correct answer is **BCAD.**

questions.question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

"We are cleaning the room."

options.text: The room is being cleaned by us.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "We are cleaning the room."
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "the room" at the beginning.
 
• Change the active verb form "are cleaning" to "is being cleaned" (present continuous passive).
 
• Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "us."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The room is being cleaned by us."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **"The room is cleaned." – Incorrect tense (simple present passive).
 
• **Option 2: **"The room has been cleaning." – Incorrect verb form (has been cleaning is not valid in passive voice).
 
• **Option 3: **"The room was cleaned." – Incorrect tense (simple past passive).
